# External Skills Documentation

Curated third-party skills vendored from upstream Git repositories via `scripts/external_skills.py` and pinned in `skills/external/manifest.json`. External skills can share a logical `--group` name with `skills/custom/` for unified workspace deployment.

```bash
python3 scripts/install_skills.py install --bucket external --workspace /path/to/project
python3 scripts/install_skills.py install --group <group> --workspace /path/to/project
python3 scripts/external_skills.py check
```

<!-- external-skills:start -->
## Domain Groups

### engineering

- [ask-matt](../../skills/external/engineering/ask-matt/SKILL.md) ([upstream](https://github.com/mattpocock/skills/tree/abeeaf95660ba9e8b7c753eb38f441ca707a8823/skills/engineering/ask-matt), `abeeaf9566`): Ask which skill or flow fits your situation. A router over the skills in this repo.
- [code-review](../../skills/external/engineering/code-review/SKILL.md) ([upstream](https://github.com/mattpocock/skills/tree/abeeaf95660ba9e8b7c753eb38f441ca707a8823/skills/engineering/code-review), `abeeaf9566`): Review the changes since a fixed point (commit, branch, tag, or merge-base) along two axes: Standards (does the code follow this repo's documented coding standards?) and Spec (does the code match what the originating issue/spec asked for?). Runs both reviews in parallel sub-agents and reports them side by side. Use when the user wants to review a branch, a PR, work-in-progress changes, or asks to \"review since X\".

Use when the user wants to design or improve a module's interface, find deepening opportunities, decide where a seam goes, make code more testable or AI-navigable, or when another skill needs the deep-module vocabulary.

Use when provisioning infrastructure, setting up credentials or CI secrets, walking an unfamiliar third-party dashboard, or running a one-off migration or cutover. Don't invoke this for steps the agent can perform itself.
